## **Verb Phrases (VP)**
<br>
.pull-left[
- a verb phrase (**VP**) consists of **a verb** and everything that **modify** it<br><br>
- generally, this includes **everything** in a sentence except the **subject** (the entity that performs the action indicated by the verb)<br><br>
- the simplest **VP** is a single verb:
.pull-left[
- *Arthur <u>ate</u>*.<br>

- *Merlin <u>left</u>*.
<br><br><br><br>

<h3><span style="color:#CC0033"><b>VP</b></span>→ V</h3>
]
.pull-right[
**VP** → V<br>

**VP** → V
]<br><br>
]
.pull-right[
<img src="../pic/1005/english.jpg" width="85%">
]

---
## **Verb Phrases (VP)**
<br>
.pull-left[
- besides the verb, **VP**s also contain any **objects** of the verb<br><br>
- <span style="color:blue"><b>direct object</b></span>: person or entity **affected** by the action indicated by the verb<br>
  <span style="color:blue"><b>direct object</b></span>s are <span style="color:blue"><b>NP</b></span>s:
  - <i>Peter <u>baked [<span style="color:blue">a cake</span>]</u></i>.<br><br>
  
- <span style="color:orange"><b>indirect object</b></span>: person or entity that **receives** something or **benefits** from the action<br>
  <span style="color:orange"><b>indirect object</b></span> can be <span style="color:green"><b>PP</b></span>s or <span style="color:blue"><b>NP</b></span>s:
  - <i>Peter <u>baked [<span style="color:blue">a cake</span>] [<span style="color:orange">for his mom</span>]</u></i>.
  - <i>Peter <u>baked [<span style="color:orange">his mom</span>] [<span style="color:blue">a cake</span>] </u></i>.
<br><br>

<h3><span style="color:#CC0033"><b>VP</b></span>→ V (NP) (NP/PP)</h3>
]
.pull-right[
<img src="../pic/1005/english.jpg" width="85%">
]

---
## **Verb Phrases (VP)**
<br>
.pull-left[
- in addition to objects, a **VP** can contain <span style="color:green"><b>adjuncts</b></span><br><br>
- they are **optional** elements that describe the **action** and therefore **modify** the verb<br><br>
- adjuncts may be <span style="color:green"><b>PP</b></span>s or <span style="color:deeppink"><b>AdvP</b></span>s:<br><br>
  - <i>The train <u>arrived [<span style="color:green">at Shanghai</span>]</u></i>.<br>
  **VP** → V <span style="color:green">PP</span><br><br>
  - <i>The train <u>arrived [<span style="color:green">quickly</span>]</u></i>.<br>
  **VP** → V <span style="color:deeppink">AdvP</span><br><br>
- a sentence can have multiple <span style="color:green"><b>adjuncts</b></span>:<br><br>
  - <i>The train <u>arrived [<span style="color:green">quickly</span>] [<span style="color:green">at Shanghai</span>]</u></i>.<br>
]
.pull-right[
<img src="../pic/1005/english.jpg" width="85%">
]

---
class: center, middle
<h1><span style="color:#CC0033"><b>VP</b></span>→ <span style="color:deeppink"><b>(AdvP+)</b></span> <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>V</b></span> <span style="color:blue"><b>(NP)</b></span> <span style="color:blue"><b>(NP)</b></span> <span style="color:deeppink"><b>(AdvP+)</b></span> <span style="color:green"><b>(PP+)</b></span> <span style="color:deeppink"><b>(AdvP+)</b></span></h1>
<br><br><br>
<div style="text-align:left">
just remember a few things:<br><br>
1. a <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>VP</b></span> always has a verb <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>head</b></span><br>
2. a <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>VP</b></span> can contain many <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>optional</b></span> things like <span style="color:blue"><b>NP</b></span>, <span style="color:green"><b>PP</b></span>, and <span style="color:deeppink"><b>AdvP</b></span> arguments and adjuncts, <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>BUT</b></span>:<br><br>
3. a <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>VP</b></span> does NOT contain the subject of the verb<br>
4. <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>VP</b></span>s will NOT directly contain an <span style="color:orange"><b>AdjP</b></span> (since AdjPs describe nouns, not verbs)<br>
5. any <span style="color:blue"><b>NP</b></span>s or <span style="color:green"><b>PP</b></span>s will always go after the verb<br>
6. objects and adjuncts will always be <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>siblings</b></span> of the verb
</div>


---
## **Tense Phrases (TP, Sentence)**
<br>
.pull-left[
**sentences** are also known as <span style="color:brown"><b>tense phrases</b></span> (<span style="color:brown"><b>TP</b></span>, or occasionally S), and it consists of:<br><br>
- <span style="color:blue"><b>NP</b></span> – a required subject<br><br>
- <span style="color:brown"><b>T</b></span> – an optional slot called "tense" that can be filled by:<br><br>
  1. modal verbs (*can*, *might*, *should...*)
  2. auxiliary verbs (*is*, *are*, *has*, *will*…)
  3. the infinitive marker *to* as in *to go*, *to see*
  4. PAST and PRESENT if there is no overt tense-marker as above<br><br>
- <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>VP</b></span> – a required verb phrase (sometimes called the predicate)
<br>
<h3><b><span style="color:brown">TP</span></b> → <span style="color:blue">NP</span></b> <b><span style="color:brown">(T)</span></b> <span style="color:#CC0033">VP</span></b></h3>
]
.pull-right[
<br>
<br><br>
<img src="../pic/1005/tense.jpg" width="90%">
]


---
## **Steps for Drawing Trees**
<br>
1. write the sentence at the bottom of the page – leave yourself **plenty of room**<br><br>
2. label the **part of speech** of each word<br><br>
3. sentences have a subject <span style="color:blue"><b>NP</b></span> and predicate **VP** – try to identify these first, and draw the subject<br><br>
4. trees should ALWAYS follow **PSR**s, so try to identify elements that can be part of rules for different phrases<br><br>
5. every <span style="color:blue"><b>noun</b></span>, <span style="color:orange"><b>adjective</b></span>, <span style="color:deeppink"><b>adverb</b></span>, <span style="color:green"><b>preposition</b></span> has its own corresponding phrase <span style="color:blue"><b>NP</b></span>, <span style="color:orange"><b>AdjP</b></span>, <span style="color:deeppink"><b>AdvP</b></span>, <span style="color:green"><b>PP</b></span><br><br>
6. smaller trees first, then figure out how they connect to the rest of the tree<br><br>
<b>some notes</b>
- VPs can have lots of elements, so figure them out last
- **pay attention to what modifies what** – any phrase that modifies a word should be its **sibling**
- because of the way English is structured, it can often be easier to start at the end and work **backwards**
